transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I guess I’m here because my eating’s gotten a little more… strict than I meant it to. It started as just trying to eat cleaner, you know, be in better shape for the lieutenant track, and I thought that was a good thing.

But lately I’ve noticed I’ll get through a shift day on like… black coffee, maybe a protein shake, and then a small dinner later, even when I know I burned way more than that. I don’t know if that sounds dramatic or not, but it’s started to feel like maybe I should talk to someone before it gets more out of hand.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently, or are you currently underweight, based on what you know is considered a healthy weight for your height?

Um… yeah, I guess so. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m falling apart or anything, but my gear and station clothes definitely hang a lot looser than they used to.

And during the fitness review they, uh… flagged my weight as being too low for my build. I know that should probably register more with me, but part of me still feels like I could trim down a little more, if that makes sense.
Do you find yourself afraid of gaining weight or doing things that actively prevent you from gaining weight, even if you know you might need to eat more?

Yeah… I mean, I wouldn’t say I’m terrified all the time or anything. But if the scale is up even, like, a pound after a big station meal or if I drank a lot of water, I get this tight feeling—almost panic.

It’s embarrassing to say, but my head goes right to, “I blew it,” and that people are going to look at me and think I’m getting soft or I’m not in control. I know that probably doesn’t sound totally rational.
Do you ever find yourself eating a very large amount of food in a short period of time, like feeling out of control with eating, or do you make yourself vomit or use laxatives to control your weight?

Um… no, not really. I mean, I don’t think so.

I don’t have times where I’m eating a huge amount and feel out of control like that. And I’m not making myself throw up or anything. Laxatives, no. That’s not… that’s not something I do.

I guess my issue is more on the other side, if that makes sense. But no, not that.

When you look in the mirror or think about your body, do you see yourself as heavier or different than what others might see, or feel like you still need to lose more weight even when others say you're too thin?

Yeah… I mean, I know other people have said I’m looking too thin, and I’m not trying to argue with them exactly.

But when I look in the mirror before work, I kind of zero in on my waist and my face—like whether they look sharp enough, if that makes sense. And if they don’t look right to me, it throws me off. I feel less… ready, I guess. Less confident, less like I’m showing up the way I’m supposed to.

I know that probably sounds kind of strange. I’m not saying I see something totally different than reality, but it feels like I still notice places where I should be leaner, even when other people are telling me the opposite.
